global_scale_contrast.interpretation: Widely separated capital tails show the source-level accounting identity clearly: higher capital carries wider physical and volatility-normalized stops and lower fixed stress cost per planned R. This contrast is heavily entangled with time and cannot establish the feedback by itself.

chronology_falsifier.interpretation: Capital rank is almost chronology rank inside the global cells, so the frozen local time-block contrast is the decision-bearing lens.

local_time_controlled_scale.interpretation: A smaller but predeclared material geometry and cost-scale effect survives within chronological blocks, so the accounting-scale observation is preserved.

hazard_and_quality_transmission.interpretation: The local stop-rate reduction is only 0.09 percentage point rather than the required two points, reaches only two of four periods and two of six components, and higher-capital local rows have worse mean stressed R. Scale does not transmit into broad favorable lifecycle economics.

preserve: the observed capital-dependent stop and cost-R accounting geometry as a diagnostic fact
the current 4% per-position and 12% aggregate risk contract

discard: the claim that higher capital broadly lowers stop hazard with nonworse normalized outcomes

decision_translation.observation: R and cost burden are scale-dependent accounting quantities, but the observed geometry does not produce a broad favorable hazard-and-quality feedback after local time control.
